patterns.signature: Right-turning drivers from the south approach vs pedestrians in the east crosswalk
patterns.summary: 4 close calls across all three cameras where a right-turning driver entered the east crosswalk while a pedestrian was in it or about to step in. Worst margin 0.7 s. In 3 of 4 the pedestrian was already crossing when the car arrived.

recommendations.name: Leading Pedestrian Interval
recommendations.why: In 3 of 4 events the pedestrian had already started crossing when the turning car arrived (EV_A1_0023, EV_A1_0060, EV_A3_0026). A head start makes pedestrians visible before turns begin.
recommendations.review_note: Suggested for traffic engineer review; not a verified design decision.

recommendations.name: Crosswalk Visibility Enhancements
recommendations.why: 1 event(s) involved a pedestrian hidden from the driver (EV_A1_0060): a parked van on the east leg blocked the sight line to the crosswalk.
recommendations.review_note: Suggested for traffic engineer review; not a verified design decision.

verification.reason: Car turns right into the crosswalk 0.7s after the pedestrian clears its path; driver did not yield.
verification.description: A green sedan turning right from the south approach cuts through the east crosswalk while a pedestrian is crossing.
contributing_factors: turning driver looking left for gaps in traffic

verification.reason: Pedestrian enters the crosswalk 1.5s after the turning car passes; the car never slowed.

disclaimer: Close calls measured from simulated footage with project thresholds (PET < 3 s or TTC < 2 s). Recommendations come only from the FHWA Proven Safety Countermeasures catalog and are suggestions for traffic engineer review.
